seo.metaDescription: Install tally-charts, import the theme, render your first chart and give it the name that screen readers need.

props.markdown: Install `tally-charts`, load its theme once and render a chart from a few rows of data. It takes about a minute.
Like React, the package reads `process.env.NODE_ENV` to turn development warnings on, so it expects a bundler that defines it (Vite, webpack, Next.js and esbuild with `define` all do).

Import the stylesheet once, near the root of your app. It defines the `--ch-*` design tokens that every chart reads for colors, type and spacing. Light and dark both work out of the box: charts follow the system setting, and a `data-ch-theme="light"` or `data-ch-theme="dark"` attribute on any ancestor forces one.
`data` is an array of plain objects, `x` and `y` name the keys to read. The props are serializable, so the same code works in a Server Component.

**A name is required.** Every chart is a `figure` that screen readers announce by name. TypeScript requires `title` or `aria-labelledby` on every chart (the type is `ChartName`), and calls from JavaScript that give neither warn in development.
If the page already has a visible heading, point the chart at it instead of repeating the text:
